Blocks.Text: Learn about the industry terms and LinkedIn-specific terminology used throughout the Talent Solutions documentation.
An ACL is a list that defines which recruiters or team members have permission to view specific jobs and applications. It controls data visibility and access rights within an organization.
An applicant is a candidate who applies to a job by submitting the job application.
Application feedback is a notification sent to applicants about the status of their job application. Examples include application viewed, resume downloaded, and application rejected.
Applicant Tracking System (ATS) is software used by employers to manage recruiting and hiring processes, including job postings, applications, candidate tracking, and interviews.
A batch call is an API request that processes multiple records in a single operation. Typically, LinkedIn recommends a maximum of 100 records per batch.
A basic job is a free job posting on LinkedIn without paid promotion features.
A candidate is a person being considered for a job opening.
A career site is an employer organization's dedicated website for listing job openings and accepting applications.
A child application is a developer application created programmatically by a partner using a parent application. Child applications are used to isolate data and traffic across individual customers.
A CRM is software that stores and manages candidate information. It syncs with LinkedIn Recruiter to export profiles and track recruiting activity.

A customer is an employer organization that recruits and hires talent. In partner integrations, a customer uses an ATS, CRM, or Job Distributor provider's software to manage their recruiting processes and is a user of at least one of LinkedIn's talent products. The partner builds integrations that enable customers to sync jobs, receive applications, and access LinkedIn features directly within their provider's product.

A developer application is an entity that provides credentials for API access. Developer applications have configured settings that determine API endpoint access, authorization capabilities, and branding via name and logo.
A full profile is a complete LinkedIn member profile containing detailed information such as work history, education, skills, certifications, and recommendations.
InMail is LinkedIn's messaging feature that allows recruiters to contact members they are not connected to.

Integration context is a URN that identifies the organization or contract for an integration and is used in API requests. It represents the LinkedIn identifiers associated with the customer using the integration.

Integration type specifies which LinkedIn product integration is being used. Examples include APPLY_CONNECT (Apply Connect integration), CSA_API (Recruiter System Connect data access), PROFILE_PLUGIN (profile viewing in ATS), ONE_CLICK_EXPORT (candidate export from Recruiter), and UNIFIED_SEARCH (search across both systems).
A job application is a submission of a candidate's information for a specific job opening.
A job distributor is a third-party service that distributes job postings to multiple job boards and platforms.
A job posting is a listing of a job opening published to attract applicants. It can be on LinkedIn, career sites, or job boards.
A job requisition is an internal record of a job opening in an ATS. It manages sourcing and hiring workflow.
A job slot is a paid job posting allocation purchased from LinkedIn that allows premium or promoted job postings with enhanced visibility.
Job state is the current status of a job posting. Values include LISTED (active and visible), CLOSED (no longer accepting applications), or UNLISTED (not visible on LinkedIn).
A member is an individual with an account on LinkedIn. A member becomes an applicant after they apply to a job posting.

OAuth 2.0 is an industry-standard protocol for authentication and authorization. LinkedIn Talent APIs use the Client Credentials Flow (2-legged OAuth) for server-to-server authentication between partner systems and LinkedIn.

One Click Export is the action in Recruiter System Connect or CRM Connect of sending a LinkedIn member's profile data from LinkedIn Recruiter to an ATS or CRM system when requested by a Recruiter user.
Onsite Apply in the Apply Connect program refers to a job application submitted directly on LinkedIn using LinkedIn's application form.
An organization is a company or business entity that has a LinkedIn page. Organizations can post jobs, manage applications, and interact with members through LinkedIn's platform.
A parent application is the main developer application under which child applications can be created for multi-tenant scenarios.
A partner is an ATS/CRM provider or job distributor that integrates with LinkedIn's APIs to serve their customers.
A premium job (also called a promoted job) is a paid job posting with enhanced visibility and promotion on LinkedIn.
A push event is a real-time notification sent from LinkedIn to a partner system via webhook when specific events occur, such as receiving a new job application.
A rate limit is the maximum number of requests allowed within a time period. Exceeding this limit returns a 429 error.
Resync is the process of updating job information between an ATS and LinkedIn to resolve inconsistencies and ensure data consistency.
A stub profile is a limited version of a LinkedIn member profile containing basic information such as name, headline, and current employer.
A confirmation, issued by LinkedIn, that a member's real-world identity or association with an organization is genuine, based on evidence such as a government ID or a corporate work email.

The set of a member's verification records shared with certified partners so recruiters can view LinkedIn-issued trust signals on an applicant without leaving the ATS. Verification data is a positive signal only; its absence carries no negative meaning.
A single verification held by a member, describing one verified dimension (identity or workplace), the method used, and when it was last verified.
